nodes.What it is: A motor supplies motion; a joint actuator packages that motor with bearings, transmission and structure. Compare brushed servomotors, steppers and brushless motors by torque-speed behaviour, mass and how they mount, rather than by their command protocol.
nodes.Prerequisites: Basic forces and units; Electronics fundamentals for robots; Smart servos & serial actuator buses for powered tests.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Established design choices, not a winner-takes-all technology. Current integration work combines motor, reducer, bearings and thermal path; this node excludes FOC firmware and serial-bus setup.
nodes.Key players: MIT robotics teaching; maxon; Open Dynamic Robot Initiative

nodes.Node: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty
nodes.What it is: Sizing means checking whether an actuator can move the actual load repeatedly, not just once at peak torque. Include gravity, acceleration, gear ratio, reflected rotor inertia and heat during the duty cycle.
nodes.Prerequisites: Electric actuator architectures: mechanical trade-offs; basic algebra and free-body diagrams; motor datasheet units.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Continuous and peak ratings remain different constraints. maxon documents temperature-dependent motor data; real winding temperature and assembly heat transfer must be measured rather than inferred from a catalogue peak.

nodes.What it is: Gears trade speed for torque while changing direction or packaging. A planetary train places smaller planet gears around a sun gear; housing, tooth count, backlash and bearing alignment affect whether it works well.
nodes.Prerequisites: Electric actuator architectures: mechanical trade-offs; basic ratios; CAD sketches.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Planetary and spur gearing are established. Printed teaching models explain reduction but their friction, tooth strength and backlash do not establish industrial actuator performance.
nodes.Key players: Harmonic Drive planetary products; MIT machine-design teaching

nodes.What it is: An eccentric input makes a lobed disc move around a ring of pins. An output mechanism removes that wobble to obtain slow rotation; tolerances, bearing loads and disc balancing matter as much as the theoretical ratio.
nodes.Prerequisites: Spur and planetary gear trains; Bearings, structures and printed load paths; CAD and design for manufacture of robot joints.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Nabtesco documents a two-stage RV mechanism. Student printed cycloidal reducers are useful experiments, not drop-in substitutes for precision commercial reducers.

nodes.What it is: A wave generator flexes a thin toothed cup into an oval so it engages a rigid ring. A small tooth-count difference gives large reduction, but flexspline fatigue, elastic twist and manufacturing accuracy constrain the design.
nodes.Prerequisites: Spur and planetary gear trains; Bearings, structures and printed load paths; material elasticity.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Harmonic Drive explains metal flexspline and wave-generator operation. Vendor zero-backlash claims do not mean infinite stiffness or that a printed educational flexspline has the same rating.

nodes.What it is: Belts and wrapped cables move torque away from the motor, reducing moving mass at a joint. Belt tension, pulley alignment and cable preload set stiffness, slip and usable travel; a capstan is not simply an unlimited-rotation cable pulley.
nodes.Prerequisites: Spur and planetary gear trains; Bearings, structures and printed load paths; safe handling of tensioned elements.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: MIT design notes discuss belt tension and capstan termination; ODRI provides pulley-based actuator assembly examples. Low apparent backlash still needs load-reversal and tension-loss testing.
nodes.Key players: Open Dynamic Robot Initiative; MIT machine-design teaching

nodes.Node: Lead screws, ball screws and linear joint packaging
nodes.What it is: A rotating screw turns motor motion into linear travel. Lead screws slide while ball screws use rolling balls; lead, guide alignment, buckling, preload and backdriving determine whether a linear joint is suitable.
nodes.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; Bearings, structures and printed load paths.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: MIT design notes contrast sliding and rolling screws and explain over-constrained guide alignment. Do not assume every screw self-locks; gravity loads need an independent retention assessment.
nodes.Key players: MIT machine-design teaching; linear-motion component designers

nodes.Node: Linkages, cams and parallel mechanism design
nodes.What it is: A linkage constrains several connected pieces to make a useful path; cams shape motion through a profile. Serial, closed-loop and parallel arrangements trade reach, stiffness and assembly complexity, while singular configurations can jam or amplify loads.
nodes.Prerequisites: Basic geometry and forces; CAD sketches. Full inverse kinematics belongs in Kinematics & dynamics.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: MIT mechanism teaching grounds joint primitives and open/closed chains. DLR uses shaped cams in variable-stiffness joints; the focus here is geometry and load paths rather than a general motion-planning node.

nodes.Node: Tendon routing, antagonism and underactuated mechanisms
nodes.What it is: Tendons pull but do not push, so routing, pretension and a return spring or opposing tendon determine movement. Underactuation uses fewer motors than joints, making the mechanical coupling useful but also harder to predict.
nodes.Prerequisites: Timing-belt and capstan transmissions; Linkages, cams and parallel mechanism design; Grasp mechanics for hand applications.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: RSS 2025 RUKA and RSS 2024 pneumatic-arm research expose routing and low-distal-mass trade-offs. This node studies transmission and coupling, not another gripper-design or dexterous-policy node.
nodes.Key players: RUKA authors; DLR; RSS pneumatic-arm authors

nodes.What it is: Backdrivability means an external load can move the actuator backwards. Transparency describes how little extra inertia and friction the mechanism adds; low gear ratio helps but does not by itself prove low friction or safe contact.
nodes.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; Spur and planetary gear trains; guarded test fixtures.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Modern Robotics explains squared gear-ratio effects on reflected inertia. MIT Cheetah actuator research grounds low-ratio design; transparency and passive safety must be measured, not inferred from current sensing.
nodes.Key players: MIT Biomimetic Robotics; Modern Robotics authors

nodes.What it is: A deliberate spring between drive and output stores energy and makes output force observable through spring deflection. The spring also introduces resonance and limits bandwidth, so stiffness selection and mechanical stops are design decisions.
nodes.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; Backdrivability, friction and mechanical transparency; elementary spring forces.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: DLR references distinguish intentional series elasticity from incidental gearbox compliance. Elasticity trades shock tolerance and energy storage against deflection and dynamics; it is not a universal improvement.
nodes.Key players: DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics; compliant-actuator researchers

nodes.What it is: Variable-stiffness hardware changes its physical spring behaviour rather than merely changing a controller gain. Cams, moving lever arms or opposing spring-loaded motors can adjust how strongly a joint resists displacement.
nodes.Prerequisites: Series-elastic actuator mechanics; Linkages, cams and parallel mechanism design; Control fundamentals for powered experiments.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: DLR David documents antagonism, BAVS and Floating Spring Joint concepts. The research question is useful stiffness range versus mass, energy and complexity, not an unsupported claim of new 2026 adoption.
nodes.Key players: DLR; authors of the variable-stiffness actuator design review

nodes.Node: Bearings, structures and printed load paths
nodes.What it is: Bearings guide rotation while the surrounding frame carries loads into the base. Shaft support, fits, fasteners and print orientation matter: a strong motor cannot rescue a flexible bracket or a bearing seat that creeps.
nodes.Prerequisites: Basic forces, moments and material elasticity; measuring tools; safe fabrication induction.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: SKF distinguishes bearing families; Prusa explains print-aware modeling. Printed prototypes need measured stiffness and fit checks; catalogue material strength is not a complete printed-part rating.
nodes.Key players: SKF; Prusa Research; ODRI hardware authors

nodes.Node: CAD and design for manufacture of robot joints
nodes.What it is: Parametric CAD describes parts using dimensions and constraints so changes remain consistent. Robot design also needs assemblies, tolerance allowances, fastener access, serviceable cable paths and a believable mass model before fabrication.
nodes.Prerequisites: Basic geometry; introductory mechanical drawing; Bearings, structures and printed load paths for loaded parts.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: FreeCAD provides parametric modeling and assembly capabilities; onshape-to-robot exports robot descriptions. CAD export is a starting model, not proof of correct inertia, friction or manufacturing tolerances.
nodes.Key players: FreeCAD contributors; onshape-to-robot maintainers; Prusa Research

nodes.What it is: Pressurized liquid or air drives a piston or contracting muscle. Force depends on pressure and effective area; seals, hoses, compressibility, pumps or compressors and leakage change the complete system, not just the actuator.
nodes.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; elementary pressure and fluid units; supervised pressure-system safety.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: RSS 2024 demonstrates a pneumatic-muscle tendon arm. Boston Dynamics retired hydraulic Atlas for an electric successor in 2024; that is one platform decision, not proof that hydraulics are obsolete.
nodes.Key players: Festo; RSS pneumatic-arm authors; Boston Dynamics

nodes.Node: Soft pneumatic actuators and compliant-body fabrication
nodes.What it is: An elastomer chamber bends or extends when inflated because its geometry constrains expansion unevenly. Molds, wall thickness, reinforcement and repeatable sealing are the mechanism, rather than a separate rigid gearbox.
nodes.Prerequisites: Hydraulic and pneumatic transmission mechanics; CAD and design for manufacture of robot joints; materials handling induction.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: The Harvard-origin Soft Robotics Toolkit documents PneuNets design, fabrication and testing. Reliable pressure-angle behaviour and fatigue remain tasks to measure; do not extrapolate a single bending video into industrial durability.
nodes.Key players: Harvard Biodesign Lab; Soft Robotics Toolkit contributors

nodes.Node: Artificial muscles: electrohydraulic and smart-material actuation
nodes.What it is: Artificial muscles change shape directly using materials or internal fluids rather than a rotating motor. Electrohydraulic pouches such as HASEL and HALVE combine electrical attraction with fluid displacement; shape-memory and piezoelectric approaches occupy different force, stroke and thermal regimes.
nodes.Prerequisites: Soft pneumatic actuators and compliant-body fabrication; material mechanics; specialist high-voltage safety before any energized electrohydraulic work.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: The 2024 HALVE paper reduces voltage relative to prior electrohydraulic actuators, but its reported 1100 V is not hobby-safe low voltage. Other smart-material families are acknowledged here, not claimed comprehensively surveyed or ready for procurement. A 2025 SMA microactuator paper demonstrates thermally controlled folding and magnetic latching; a PNAS origami arm demonstrates magnetic actuation. These are research-specific mechanisms, not interchangeable muscles.
nodes.Key players: ETH Zurich Soft Robotics Lab; HALVE paper authors

nodes.Node: Integrated legged and humanoid joint co-design
nodes.What it is: A useful leg or humanoid joint balances torque, speed, mass, cooling, travel, impact tolerance and maintenance. Quasi-direct drive uses a relatively low reduction ratio with a torque-dense motor; parallel links or remote drives offer other packaging trade-offs.
nodes.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; Bearings, structures and printed load paths; Backdrivability, friction and mechanical transparency; BLDC motor control & field-oriented control (FOC) for powered drives.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ODRI exposes module assembly and test stands; ToddlerBot documents maintainable hardware and 2025/2026 releases. Atlas 2026 manufacturer statements give ecosystem context, not public internal actuator specs or independently verified deployment performance.
nodes.Key players: Open Dynamic Robot Initiative; Stanford ToddlerBot team; MIT Biomimetic Robotics; Boston Dynamics

robots_models.Name: RUKA
Knowledge nodes: Tendon routing, antagonism and underactuated mechanisms

robots_models.Why it matters: Reference for tendon routing and low-cost material trade-offs, not a duplicate grippers knowledge node.

robots_models.Name: DLR David variable-stiffness joints
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics

robots_models.Name: Festo DMSP fluidic muscle
robots_models.Price / access: Commercial configurable product; pressure supply, valves and safety equipment are additional; complete price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Single-acting pulling polymer tensile actuator with contraction characteristics; variant-specific pressure/force ratings require its datasheet.
robots_models.Why it matters: A concrete pneumatic-muscle example with system-level supply requirements.

robots_models.Name: PneuNets bending-actuator toolkit

robots_models.Price / access: Public fabrication and testing documentation; file-specific reuse license and complete build cost unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Elastomer pneumatic chamber design, molding, modeling and testing resources; this is a fabrication reference, not a rigid-arm simulator.
robots_models.Why it matters: A reproducible starting point for learning compliant-body fabrication.

robots_models.Why it matters: Useful for inspecting serviceability, bearing-based idlers and robot joint packaging; not a first full-humanoid procurement recommendation.

top3.Node: CAD and design for manufacture of robot joints
top3.justification: Highest accessibility (5), visible moving assemblies and direct usefulness for every SO-101 or new joint adaptation. FreeCAD gives a zero-incremental-hardware start; drawings and fit checks avoid premature purchases. High ecosystem leverage through reusable CAD-to-robot models, without assuming the robot-learning wedge is proven.

Accessibility 4, an immediately visible remote-drive mechanism, and relevance to ODRI and low-moving-mass robots. A hand-driven belt rig targets <€500 with shared tools; it teaches tension and backlash before expensive custom actuators. Current delivered cost remains unknown.

top3.Node: Linkages, cams and parallel mechanism design
top3.justification: Accessibility 4 and a strong filmable motion transformation from cardboard or CAD, before motor procurement. Linkage reasoning transfers to humanoid packaging and tendon systems; very low initial materials cost offers a better first risk/reward than a complete legged robot or high-voltage muscle.
